purpose: A background image paints behind content; it does not give the element its size.

purpose: Adjacent vertical margins of ordinary block siblings can collapse. With two positive margins, the gap is the larger one, not their sum.

.stack { display: flow-root; } .first, .second { height: 20px; } .first { margin-bottom: 24px; } .second { margin-top: 16px; }

purpose: A float lets following inline content wrap alongside it. flow-root gives the parent a new block formatting context that encloses its floats.

.demo { writing-mode: horizontal-tb; direction: ltr; }

purpose: Flex alignment has two axes. align-items sets the items’ cross-axis alignment; align-self can override it for one item.

.demo { writing-mode: horizontal-tb; direction: ltr; }

.grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 100px 100px; grid-template-rows: 40px; grid-auto-rows: 60px; gap: 0; }

.banner { width: 240px; height: 80px; background-image: linear-gradient(to right, navy 0%, teal 100%); } .banner span { color: white; background: black; }

purpose: Supply a horizontal translation transform
inputsOrValues: 0px, one length argument
resultOrEffect: Zero visual translation, but a non-none transform establishes a fixed-position containing block
visibleExample:
.demo { writing-mode: horizontal-tb; direction: ltr; }
.host { height: 100px; } .badge { position: fixed; top: 10px; left: 12px; width: 60px; height: 20px; background: navy; color: white; } .host { transform: translateX(0px); position: relative; margin-left: 30px; }
syntaxBreakdown: transform: translateX(0px); transform is the property. translateX is the CSS transform function. Its parentheses enclose the horizontal displacement. It is not a JavaScript call.
kind: CSS value function; not JavaScript callable

purpose: var(--ink, teal) substitutes the custom property --ink when it has a usable variable value; if it is missing, the fallback teal is substituted. A present value can still be invalid for the receiving property.
inputsOrValues: The first argument is the custom-property name; the comma starts the fallback. Here --ink is absent, so color receives teal. If --ink is defined as 12px, var substitutes 12px: that is invalid for color. The browser does not then retry the earlier purple declaration or the teal fallback. For this inherited property the result inherits navy from the parent. This is invalidity at computed-value time, after the cascade chose the declaration.
resultOrEffect: The fallback argument supplies tokens when the referenced custom property cannot supply them.

purpose: @supports tests whether the browser accepts a CSS declaration. Start with a usable ordinary layout, then enhance it when a feature is supported. Acceptance does not certify a complete accessible design or absence of rendering bugs.
inputsOrValues: @supports (display: grid) encloses rules inside braces. The condition asks about the property-value pair, not whether a particular element currently uses it. CSS.supports in the supplied check is test infrastructure for comparing the browser’s answer, not learner JavaScript to write. An invented value makes this condition false; the base rule still applies.
resultOrEffect: An @supports rule applies enclosed declarations when its support condition matches.

purpose: A transition animates a change between old and new property values. It does not create the state change itself. Here adding the muted class changes opacity; the transition smooths that change when motion is allowed.
inputsOrValues: transition: opacity 0.08s linear names the property, duration in seconds, and constant-speed timing. opacity: 0.4 makes the whole button partly transparent; it does not disable its action. The reduced-motion media query sets the duration to zero when the person requests reduced motion. The supplied test adds the class, waits for actual animations to finish, checks the endpoint, and removes the class; you only write CSS.
resultOrEffect: A CSS transition interpolates a property change over a duration when the property supports it.

purpose: prefers-color-scheme asks about the person’s light/dark preference. color-scheme tells the browser which scheme an element supports, helping native controls use an appropriate appearance. It does not automatically recolor every author background or text rule.
inputsOrValues: The base panel is explicitly light. The dark media branch changes both authored colors and the color-scheme value. The input keeps its native behavior. Checks verify the currently active browser preference only; this preview does not switch operating-system settings. High-contrast/forced-color mechanics are a separate topic, and meaning must not depend on color alone.
resultOrEffect: A media preference can select author styles while color-scheme informs browser-provided appearance.

purpose: @media print supplies styles for printed output or print preview. A screen toolbar can be useful on screen but waste space on paper. Keep the report itself in the document and hide only screen-only controls in print.
inputsOrValues: The media type print is not a narrow viewport query. display: none inside this print branch removes the toolbar’s print layout space; outside print, its ordinary rule remains. Explicit dark text and an uncolored background can improve legibility, but exact page breaks, margins, color reproduction and printer settings still vary. This lesson is a local companion: the app does not render or grade print output.
resultOrEffect: Rules under @media print apply to print presentation rather than ordinary screen layout.

purpose: When CSS does not look right, ask in order: did the stylesheet load, does the selector match, is the declaration valid, and which cascade rule wins? Then inspect layout geometry rather than assuming a computed value guarantees the whole page looks right.
inputsOrValues: In browser developer tools, the Elements/Inspector style panel shows matched rules and overridden declarations; the Computed panel shows resolved values. Here .notice has greater specificity than p within the same origin/layer/importance, so teal wins even though p comes later. A misspelled class selector would not match at all. This exercise fixes a small selector/cascade problem; it does not automate or replace the developer-tools investigation.
resultOrEffect: A debugging sequence separates loading, matching, validity, cascade and layout questions.

purpose: @font-face names a font resource that font-family can request. A fallback family remains important while loading or when a resource fails. This tiny original teaching font has only A, B and a space; it is a loading demonstration, not a full reading font or a font-design course.
inputsOrValues: font-family inside @font-face gives the face its CSS name. src supplies a URL and format hint; url() names the encoded local resource and format("truetype") describes its file format. font-weight and font-style describe which face it is, not an element’s requested appearance. font-display: swap permits fallback text while the face loads. The long data URL is supplied font bytes, not CSS syntax to memorize. The sample rule requests the named face with monospace fallback. Actual loading and glyph width are checked, not merely a family-name string.
resultOrEffect: @font-face associates a CSS face name and descriptors with a font resource.

purpose: display: none removes an element’s layout box. visibility: hidden hides it while its layout space remains. opacity: 0 makes it transparent but does not by itself remove its box, pointer hit testing or keyboard focusability.
inputsOrValues: The two buttons are flex items with fixed widths. Hiding the first with visibility preserves the second button’s position. Changing that declaration to display: none removes its box, so the second moves to the start. Opacity is not a safe shortcut for disabling a control: a transparent control can still act. These properties also differ for accessibility exposure; this geometry exercise is not a complete assistive-technology test.
resultOrEffect: Visibility can hide painting while display:none removes an element’s layout box.

purpose: For normal author declarations, later layers outrank earlier layers. For important author declarations, that layer order reverses: an earlier layer outranks a later one. This comparison stays within the same origin and excludes active transitions.
inputsOrValues: !important is a declaration flag after the value and before the semicolon, not part of the color. @layer base, theme establishes the order before the rules. Both declarations here are important, so base wins even though theme appears later. Removing both flags restores normal layer order and theme wins. User and browser important origins have their own precedence; do not describe this as a universal strongest-rule trick.
resultOrEffect: Important declarations use the opposite layer order from normal declarations within an origin.

purpose: A mobile-first layout starts with a useful narrow arrangement, then adds columns when enough viewport space is available. min-width includes the boundary value and larger widths. This is about available space, not detecting a particular device brand.
inputsOrValues: The base grid has one flexible column. At 600 CSS pixels or more, the media query replaces it with two equal flexible columns. Keep source order sensible in both arrangements. The preview uses its iframe viewport, not the full app width. A real mobile document also needs the viewport metadata taught in HTML; see the HTML viewport lesson rather than treating CSS as a substitute for that document setting.
resultOrEffect: A narrow base layout gains space-dependent enhancements through minimum-width queries.

purpose: Native form controls have browser-provided appearances and do not always inherit page typography in the way ordinary text does. Explicit font: inherit can make their text consistent while preserving their native editing and activation behavior.
inputsOrValues: font: inherit copies the parent’s computed font settings. border-box makes the declared input width include padding and border. min-height reserves room without pretending that one height fits every language or zoom setting. Keep the label association, name and button type in HTML. Do not remove native appearance or focus indicators merely to make the control look like a painted rectangle; appearance can vary across browsers.
resultOrEffect: Explicit font inheritance can align form-control text with its surrounding form.
